answer.headline: No exact annual shop rent can be quoted for an unspecified unit, and profit cannot be guaranteed; here is what research does and does not support.

sections.title: Why an exact annual rent is not available from our research

items.text: The curated evidence returned for Dubai and Abu Dhabi covers competitor branch locations, not shop leases; the only location record obtained describes Al Wahda Mall in Abu Dhabi as a retail centre with a Lulu Hypermarket and multiple dining options, and explicitly flags that no verified shop rent, footfall, customer mix or demand estimate is established. Rents for a specific retail unit are transaction-specific, so a single exact annual figure for an unspecified shop cannot be quoted without the unit, area, size, frontage, term and landlord terms.
No returned record in this turn contains a verified rent or lease figure for any unit in Dubai or Abu Dhabi; absence of a match is a research gap, not evidence that rents are any particular level.

Practical route to an exact annual rent: run two targeted web searches (public listings for a specific district, e.g. food-and-beverage retail units), then inspect the original listing pages and confirm with the mall/free-zone/landlord or a licensed broker, since snippets alone cannot establish rent or contractual terms.

No one can guarantee restaurant profit, and nothing in the evidence supports a profit claim: branch listings for competitors show only that businesses list those addresses, and the qualifiers state that presence does not establish sales, market share or footfall.

Your profile has no startup budget, monthly rent budget, branch format, target audience or positioning set, and per-order revenue, food, packaging, other variable costs, delivery share and commission, fixed costs and operating days are all unknown. Because all eight numeric inputs required for contribution and break-even analysis are missing, no unit-economics calculation is presented here.

Instead of a rent quote or profit assurance, the defensible output is a coverage-and-cost test: get at least two or three real unit quotes per candidate district, then model contribution per order and monthly break-even with actual supplier and commission terms.

sections.title: Competitive context that should shape site selection

items.text: Observed pizza-format listings include Al Ghurair Centre (Al Muraqqabat) and Deira City Centre (Port Saeed) in Dubai, and Abu Dhabi Mall (Al Zahiyah) plus ADNOC 913 Khalidiya in Abu Dhabi.

Further Dubai pizza listings appear at Al Barsha Mall and Marina Diamond near Dubai Marina Metro Station; these are listing locations only, and proximity between two addresses does not establish a shared delivery catchment, so treat each as a separate site to verify.

Street-food/kebab-adjacent operators to benchmark against include Allo Beirut on Hessa Street (Al Barsha), Dubai, advertising delivery until 4 AM, and Al Najda Street (Al Danah), Abu Dhabi; the source's own qualifier notes advertised hours do not establish overnight demand in a proposed catchment.

Differentiation to test rather than assume: lead with the Jordanian meat-forward pizza and kebab sandwich identity, and probe whether a Jordanian provenance angle, portion size or late-hour service is a real gap in each specific district during site visits and trial orders.

sections.title: Research gaps to close before any commitment

items.text: Gaps: no verified shop rents, service charges, fit-out costs, mall/free-zone fees, supplier quotes, delivery commission rates, licence requirements or category demand in either city from the records returned in this turn.

Two web searches could be run for public retail-unit listings in a named Dubai district and a named Abu Dhabi district; search results would be uninspected leads, not verified rents, so the original pages and the landlord/broker must be checked directly.
